newsitem.title: MOZAMBIQUE: Disc-jockey who signalled Portuguese revolt dies.
newsitem.headline: Disc-jockey who signalled Portuguese revolt dies.

text.p: A Mozambican disc-jockey who signalled the start of the Portuguese revolution with a song died in a South African clinic on Wednesday after a long illness, Radio Mozambique announced. He was 52.
On April 25, 1974, journalist and broadcaster Teodomiro Leite de Vasconcelos placed a record on the turntable at the catholic radio station in Lisbon where he worked.
By arrangement with revolutionary officers, the song, Grandola Vila Morena, was the signal for troops who opposed the fascist regime to take to the streets and seize power.
Vasconcelos later became director general of state-run Radio Mozambique.
